name: Unverified_b5cb
rootCause: An unverified contract (the "victim" at 0xB5CB0555c4A333543DbE0b219923C7B3e9D84a87) exposed a privileged function (selector 0x94655f2b) that lacked any caller authorization check. Anyone could invoke it with attacker-controlled parameters to move/extract the victim's token holdings to an arbitrary recipient. The PoC simply replays seven raw calls with the captured calldata, each draining a different asset held by the contract (WBNB, ETH proxy token, USDT, several upgradeable-proxy tokens) to the attacker address 0xd5c6...122c, for ~2M USD total. The root cause is missing access control on a sensitive function that performs token transfers / swaps on behalf of the contract, allowing an external attacker to drain its balances.
